lines.say: Six reasons nobody can copy Israel.
In nineteen ninety, Michael Porter drew a diamond for why countries win.
Corner one, people. Half of adults have a degree, and army tech units train them young.
Corner two, demand. Ten million people is a tiny market, so startups go global from day one.
That's why high tech is fifty eight percent of exports.
Corner three, the cluster. Over five hundred multinationals operate here.
Corner four, rivalry. About seven hundred seventy five new startups in 2025, all fighting for talent.
Then two outside forces. Government: in nineteen ninety three, Yozma put a hundred million dollars into venture capital.
Today, six point eight percent of the economy goes to research. Highest in the OECD.
And chance. When the Soviet Union fell, almost nine hundred thousand people came, many of them engineers.
The weak spot? High tech is only about one in nine jobs.
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
Six forces, feeding each other. That's why nobody can just copy Israel.

caption_en:
Michael Porter wrote the playbook for why countries win. Israel checks every box but one.

Porter's Diamond (The Competitive Advantage of Nations, 1990), applied to Israel:
1. Factor conditions, people: about half of adults hold a degree (OECD Education at a Glance, 2023), and army tech units train them young.
2. Demand: a home market of 10.2 million (CBS) forces startups to go global from day one. High tech is 58% of exports (Israel Innovation Authority, 2026).
3. Related industries: 511 multinationals operate here (Innovation Authority, 2026).
4. Rivalry: about 775 new startups were founded in 2025 (Innovation Authority).
5. Government: Yozma (1993) put $100 million into venture capital. R&D is 6.8% of GDP, the highest in the OECD (OECD MSTI, 2024 data).
6. Chance: almost 900,000 people came from the former Soviet Union in 1989 to 2000 (CBS), many of them engineers.

The weak spot: high tech is 11.4% of jobs but 58% of exports. A strong diamond on a narrow base.

Which corner would you strengthen first? Tell me in the comments.
